repo_prior_art.cite: none; the only other active eid core is eid_periodic_hedge_memory_frontier, on periodic-ADMG hedge memory rather than covariance-environment replacement.

published_prior_art.cite: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1 gives the all-honest iff criterion; ShenEtAl2020JDSEM and AkhavanEtAl2019GeometryJD provide robust-JD procedures, not an exact worst-case whole-slot replacement radius with a legal BACKSHIFT converse.

RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Corollary 2(ii) gives generic all-continuous identifiability; PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift concerns sparse mechanism changes, not the stated affine-occupancy formula under slot replacement.
AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID motivates identification-robust confidence sets; the displayed coverage inclusion is a BACKSHIFT-specific inversion corollary rather than a new general inference frontier.

Afsari2008JDSensitivity is local selected-family sensitivity and AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID is general weak-identification inference; neither supplies rational affine-minor certificates across candidate honest subsets.

novelty_flags.label: thm:sharp-replacement-radius / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: Add ShenEtAl2020JDSEM (robust ℓ1 joint diagonalization of second-order covariance slabs with outliers) and distinguish its anchored-network, algorithmic model from whole-environment replacement; it is a closer robust-JD comparator than the survey presently records.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:sharp-replacement-radius / ass:invariant-noise-interior
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The sharp converse is asserted only on the interior invariant-noise class Ω ∈ S++p, not on the full PSD-noise BACKSHIFT class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Exact replacement radius conditional on Ω ∈ S++p; the c=0 BACKSHIFT result is used only as a restricted sanity reduction.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: def:subset-consensus and oeq:certified-uniform-inference
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Subset enumeration assumes a full-solution feasibility oracle and is not an implemented terminating solver.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Only an oracle reduction is settled; certification, implementable feasibility, and quantitative uniform contraction remain the open target.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3-4, equations (5)-(10); p. 4, Theorem 1 and Corollary 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The proceedings define the invariant-noise covariance relation and normalized diagonalizer, prove unique population minimization iff the pairwise intervention-variance determinant condition holds, and give almost-sure generic identifiability with at least three continuously randomized environments.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1111.7088 preprint; cited IEEE journal version was not directly accessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible author version describes a general uniqueness characterization for non-unitary matrix joint diagonalization; no primary-version formula mismatch was asserted.
The paper updates a retained target-matrix set by a thresholded geometric distance and evaluates the outlier procedure in simulations; it does not state an adversarial identifiability radius.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, Corollary 4.2; p. 6, Theorem 5.3 and Corollary 5.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves bivariate identifiability under sparse mechanism shifts and high-probability recovery of a DAG under its probabilistic sparse-mechanism model; it does not analyze affine occupancy or adversarial covariance-slot replacement.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2007.14034 author version corresponding to SIAM JMAA 43(2), 2022
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives a positive-definite feasibility characterization and numerical algorithm for simultaneous diagonalization by congruence of one complete Hermitian family.

source_verification_receipts.version: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 30(3), 2008
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited article is a sensitivity-analysis paper for nonorthogonal matrix joint diagonalization, supporting its use as a local-conditioning comparator.

source_verification_receipts.version: Cowles Discussion Paper 1824R, revised November 2012; corresponding Journal of Econometrics 173(1), 2013 publication
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible version studies estimators, tests, and confidence sets under sporadic identification failure; no claim was made that it treats corrupted BACKSHIFT subset selection.

source_verification_receipts.version: IEEE Transactions on Signal and Information Processing over Networks 6, 2020
source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1, abstract; pp. 5-6, Section III-C and equations (27)-(28)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops robust ℓ1 joint diagonalization of local second-order covariance matrices modeled as containing outlier components, but its exact-identification theorem concerns an anchored network model rather than a BACKSHIFT replacement radius.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Shen, Fu, Giannakis, and Sidiropoulos (2020) to related work and state explicitly why sparse residual corruption of covariance slabs neither subsumes nor yields the proposed whole-slot minimax radius.
Split the sharp theorem’s directions in the exposition, marking Ω ≻ 0 as needed only for the legal-converse construction and retaining the PSD class for the uniqueness direction.
Add a worked nontrivial sparse support design at m=2c+3 for p≥3 that computes all pairwise incidence counts and the resulting radius.

recommended_next_step: Revise the literature comparison to include the omitted robust covariance-slab JD result, then advance the conditional field-tier radius kernel to Stage 0.
